translationRepairs: To find tuoke, apply this standard.
To find waxing-and-waning, apply this standard.
Chinese 求朏朒准此 is the waxing-and-waning inequality procedure; "tuoke" is a corrupted gloss, and "waxing-and-waning" restores the technical term.

To find the fixed tuoke number for month-beginnings, quarter-moons, and full moons entering qi-periods: for each, multiply the minor remainder of the qi-period entered by its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by the pivot divisor for one—that is obtained.

To find the fixed waxing-and-waning number for month-beginnings, quarter-moons, and full moons entering qi-periods: for each, multiply the minor remainder of the qi-period entered by its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by the pivot divisor for one—that is obtained.
Chinese 入氣朏朒定數 names the fixed waxing-and-waning number; replacing corrupted "tuoke" with "waxing-and-waning" matches the source.
To find month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon entry into rotation tuoke.
To find month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon entry into rotation waxing-and-waning.
Heading 求朔弦望入轉朏朒 concerns rotation waxing-and-waning; "tuoke" is not a valid rendering of 朏朒.

Fixed value: set the rotation remainder entered, multiply by its daily gain-and-loss rate, divide by the pivot divisor, and apply gain or loss to the lower tuoke accumulation below to obtain the fixed value.

Fixed value: set the rotation remainder entered, multiply by its daily gain-and-loss rate, divide by the pivot divisor, and apply gain or loss to the lower waxing-and-waning accumulation below to obtain the fixed value.
Chinese 其下朏朒積 is the lower waxing-and-waning accumulation; "tuoke accumulation" misnames the technical term.

Fixed number: set the rotation remainder entered; multiply its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by the pivot divisor for one; what is obtained is used to gain and lose its lower tuoke accumulation for the fixed number.

Fixed number: set the rotation remainder entered; multiply its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by the pivot divisor for one; what is obtained is used to gain and lose its lower waxing-and-waning accumulation for the fixed number.
Literal likewise has 朏朒積; "waxing-and-waning accumulation" correctly replaces corrupted "tuoke".
If the remainder within the four sevens falls below the initial number, multiply by the initial rate, divide by the initial number, and apply gain or loss to tuoke for the fixed value.
If the remainder within the four sevens falls below the initial number, multiply by the initial rate, divide by the initial number, and apply gain or loss to waxing-and-waning for the fixed value.
Chinese 以損益朏朒 applies gain or loss to the waxing-and-waning value; "tuoke" obscures that term.
If within the four sevens the remainder is below the initial number, multiply by the initial rate; divide by the initial number for one; use to gain and lose tuoke for the fixed number.
If within the four sevens the remainder is below the initial number, multiply by the initial rate; divide by the initial number for one; use to gain and lose waxing-and-waning for the fixed number.
Same 損益朏朒; literal "waxing-and-waning" restores the correct calendrical term.

If above the initial number, subtract the initial number, multiply the remainder by the final rate and divide by the final number, subtract from the initial rate, add the remainder to tuoke, and each yields a fixed value.

If above the initial number, subtract the initial number, multiply the remainder by the final rate and divide by the final number, subtract from the initial rate, add the remainder to waxing-and-waning, and each yields a fixed value.
Chinese 餘加朏朒 adds the remainder to the waxing-and-waning quantity; "tuoke" is a corrupted romanization.

If above the initial number, subtract the initial number; multiply the remainder by the final rate; divide by the final number for one; use to subtract from the initial rate; add the remainder to tuoke—each becomes a fixed number.

If above the initial number, subtract the initial number; multiply the remainder by the final rate; divide by the final number for one; use to subtract from the initial rate; add the remainder to waxing-and-waning—each becomes a fixed number.
Literal 餘加朏朒 likewise requires waxing-and-waning, not "tuoke".
If within day 14 the remainder is above the initial number, subtract the initial number, multiply the remainder by the final rate and divide by the final number to obtain the tuoke fixed value.
If within day 14 the remainder is above the initial number, subtract the initial number, multiply the remainder by the final rate and divide by the final number to obtain the waxing fixed value.
Chinese here is 為朏定數 (waxing fixed value only), not full 朏朒; "tuoke" is wrong, but proposed "waxing-and-waning" overreads 朒 into the phrase.
If within day 14 the remainder is above the initial number, subtract the initial number; multiply the remainder by the final rate; divide by the final number for one—that is the tuoke fixed number.
If within day 14 the remainder is above the initial number, subtract the initial number; multiply the remainder by the final rate; divide by the final number for one—that is the waxing fixed number.
Source 為朏定數 names only 朏 (waxing); replacing "tuoke" with "waxing-and-waning" invents the waning half absent from this unit.

To find fixed days for month-beginnings and full moons: for each apply the fixed waxing-and-waning values from qi-period and rotation entry—subtract tuoke and add tuoke to the minor remainder for month-beginning, quarter-moon, or full moon, advance or retreat the major remainder if full or short, count from jiazi outward, and obtain the fixed day and remainder.

To find fixed days for month-beginnings and full moons: for each apply the fixed waxing-and-waning values from qi-period and rotation entry—subtract waxing and add waning to the minor remainder for month-beginning, quarter-moon, or full moon, advance or retreat the major remainder if full or short, count from jiazi outward, and obtain the fixed day and remainder.
Chinese 朏減朒加 distinguishes subtract 朏 (waxing) and add 朒 (waning); collapsing both into "waxing-and-waning" erases that opposition, though "tuoke" was also wrong.

To find fixed month-beginning and full-moon days: for each use entry into qi-period and entry into rotation tuoke fixed numbers—tuoke subtracts and tuoke adds to the month-beginning, quarter-moon, or full-moon minor remainder; if full or insufficient, advance or retreat the major remainder; count from jiazi outward—each obtains the fixed day and remainder.

To find fixed month-beginning and full-moon days: for each use entry into qi-period and entry into rotation waxing-and-waning fixed numbers—waxing subtracts and waning adds to the month-beginning, quarter-moon, or full-moon minor remainder; if full or insufficient, advance or retreat the major remainder; count from jiazi outward—each obtains the fixed day and remainder.
Phrase 朏朒定數…朏減朒加 needs "waxing-and-waning fixed numbers" plus distinct "waxing subtracts and waning adds"; the proposal's identical "waxing-and-waning" twice loses 朏/朒 polarity.

To seek the next crossing thereby, add crossing-end day and remainder seconds; when qi-divisor and remainder seconds are full remove them; the remainder is mean crossing entry into its qi-period day and remainder seconds; if seeking its qi-period tuoke fixed number, enter as in the procedure for month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon mean days—each obtains what is sought.

To seek the next crossing thereby, add crossing-end day and remainder seconds; when qi-divisor and remainder seconds are full remove them; the remainder is mean crossing entry into its qi-period day and remainder seconds; if seeking its qi-period waxing-and-waning fixed number, enter as in the procedure for month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon mean days—each obtains what is sought.
Chinese 其氣朏朒定數 is the qi-period waxing-and-waning fixed number; "tuoke" is a corrupted gloss.

To find the fixed waxing-and-waning value for mean crossing entering rotation: set the qi-period remainder entered, add midnight rotation remainder for that day, multiply by daily gain-and-loss rate and divide by the pivot divisor, apply gain or loss to the lower tuoke accumulation, then multiply by crossing rate and divide by crossing number to obtain the fixed value.

To find the fixed waxing-and-waning value for mean crossing entering rotation: set the qi-period remainder entered, add midnight rotation remainder for that day, multiply by daily gain-and-loss rate and divide by the pivot divisor, apply gain or loss to the lower waxing-and-waning accumulation, then multiply by crossing rate and divide by crossing number to obtain the fixed value.
Chinese 其下朏朒積 is the lower waxing-and-waning accumulation; replacing residual "tuoke" is correct.

To find mean-crossing entry into rotation tuoke fixed number: set the qi-period remainder entered; add its day's midnight entry into rotation remainder; multiply by its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by pivot divisor for one; what is obtained is used to gain and lose its lower tuoke accumulation; then multiply by crossing rate; divide by crossing number for one—for the fixed number.

To find mean-crossing entry into rotation waxing-and-waning fixed number: set the qi-period remainder entered; add its day's midnight entry into rotation remainder; multiply by its daily gain-and-loss rate; divide by pivot divisor for one; what is obtained is used to gain and lose its lower waxing-and-waning accumulation; then multiply by crossing rate; divide by crossing number for one—for the fixed number.
Literal 入轉朏朒定數 and 朏朒積 both require waxing-and-waning, not "tuoke".

To find proper-crossing entry into qi-periods: apply fixed waxing-and-waning from mean crossing and rotation entry—subtract tuoke and add tuoke to mean-crossing qi-period remainder, advance or retreat the day if full or short, and obtain proper-crossing entry day and remainder in seconds.

To find proper-crossing entry into qi-periods: apply fixed waxing-and-waning from mean crossing and rotation entry—subtract waxing and add waning to mean-crossing qi-period remainder, advance or retreat the day if full or short, and obtain proper-crossing entry day and remainder in seconds.
Chinese 朏減朒加 again opposes waxing subtract and waning add; proposed twin "waxing-and-waning" phrases fail to keep that polarity.

To find proper-crossing entry into qi-periods: use mean-crossing entry into qi-periods and entry into rotation tuoke fixed number—tuoke subtracts and tuoke adds to mean-crossing entry into qi-period remainder; if full or insufficient advance or retreat its day—that is proper-crossing entry into qi-period day and remainder seconds.

To find proper-crossing entry into qi-periods: use mean-crossing entry into qi-periods and entry into rotation waxing-and-waning fixed number—waxing subtracts and waning adds to mean-crossing entry into qi-period remainder; if full or insufficient advance or retreat its day—that is proper-crossing entry into qi-period day and remainder seconds.
Source has 入轉朏朒定數 then 朏減朒加; fix "tuoke" but keep waxing/waning as separate operators.

Set the qi-period day entered simplified parts; enter as in the procedure for waxing-and-waning—that is obtained.

When annotating the calendar, observe the month-beginning minor remainder; if the sun's entry parts are already reached, advance one day, but if the month-beginning is fixed and an eclipse should be visible, do not advance that month-beginning.

When annotating the calendar, observe the month-beginning minor remainder; if it is already at or above the sunset parts, advance one day, but if the month-beginning is fixed and an eclipse should be visible, do not advance that month-beginning.
日入分 paired with following 日出分 is sunset parts; "sun's entry parts" misreads 日入, and 已上 means at or above.

Whenever annotating the calendar, observe the month-beginning minor remainder; if the day's entry parts are already reached, advance one day; if the month-beginning should be fixed and an eclipse is expected to be visible, that month-beginning is not advanced.

Whenever annotating the calendar, observe the month-beginning minor remainder; if it is already at or above the sunset parts, advance one day; if the month-beginning should be fixed and an eclipse is expected to be visible, that month-beginning is not advanced.
Same 日入分 is sunset parts, not "day's entry parts"; the proposed literal matches the calendrical sense.

To find dawn and dusk moon for each day: start from month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon values, add each day's fixed rotation degree and parts, discard by lodge sequence, and obtain dawn and dusk moon for each day.

To find dawn and dusk moon for each day: start from month-beginning, quarter-moon, and full-moon values, add each day's fixed rotation degree and parts, discard by the excess–deficit sequence, and obtain dawn and dusk moon for each day.
Chinese 盈縮次去之 is discard by the excess–deficit sequence just set up; lodge sequence would be 宿次.

To find each day's dawn and dusk parts, sun-out and sun-in parts, and half-day parts: take each day's message fixed number; after spring equinox add 1,853 deficient, after autumn equinox subtract 2,912 deficient—each is that day's dawn parts;

Song calendrical 少 after an integer marks one-quarter (¼), matching the idiomatic 1,853¼ / 2,912¼; "deficient" is the wrong sense of 少.
